articles.title: World’s top court finds Myanmar guilty of genocide against Rohingya
The U.N.'s top court rules Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya
Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingya minority, world’s top court rules

events.summary: The International Court of Justice delivered its judgment finding Myanmar responsible for genocide against the ethnic Rohingya in the case of The Gambia v. Myanmar. This represents the first such ruling by the UN's principal judicial organ on the application of the Genocide Convention against the country.
events.why: A definitive genocide ruling by the world's highest court establishes binding state responsibility and sets a major international legal precedent.

articles.title: Ukraine updates: Russian attack 'one of largest,' Zelenskyy says

events.summary: President Zelenskyy reported that Russia launched one of its largest aerial attacks against Ukraine since the war began. Poland described the incident as a provocation after two missiles struck inside the NATO member country.
events.why: Missile strikes landing inside a NATO member state heighten the imminent risk of regional escalation and military conflict.

articles.title: COP31: UN Climate summit enters final phase with no deal in sight

events.summary: COP31 negotiations have entered their final phase with countries remaining divided on strategies to combat global warming. A newly released draft declaration omits any mention of phasing out fossil fuels.
events.why: Excluding fossil fuel phaseout language from the UN climate text undermines binding multilateral efforts to reduce global emissions.

articles.title: Myanmar genocide ruling: Rohingya say struggle for justice not over

events.summary: The International Court of Justice found Myanmar responsible for genocide against the Rohingya and mandated reparations and restitution. While Rohingya community members welcomed the verdict, they acknowledged enforcement will be difficult.
events.why: The definitive ruling establishes state accountability for genocide under international law and orders legal restitution for the victims.

articles.title: WFP plans to assist 91 million in 2027 as hunger crisis deepens

events.summary: The World Food Programme announced it will need $12.1 billion to provide assistance to 91 million people next year. The agency warned that persistent funding shortfalls could leave millions more hungry as another global food crisis looms.
events.why: Massive funding gaps in emergency food aid threaten the survival of tens of millions amid acute global food insecurity.

articles.title: ‘Losing the battle’: AI hands predators new ways to target children

events.summary: Senior UN officials warned that artificial intelligence is providing predators and criminal networks new tools to groom, extort, and exploit children. Protection efforts are currently failing to keep pace with these evolving technologies.
events.why: Rapid technological advances in AI are outpacing existing legal and regulatory child protection frameworks globally.

articles.title: COP31: Countries demand stronger climate deal as talks in Antalya reach final day

events.summary: A coalition of countries across Europe, Africa, Latin America, and the Pacific has challenged the draft COP31 agreement in Antalya, demanding explicit commitments on fossil fuels and stronger climate finance. As the summit reaches its final day, tensions have escalated amid warnings the conference could fail.
events.why: Disagreements over fossil fuel phaseout and climate financing directly impact the enforceability and ambition of global climate agreements.

articles.title: COP31: Ambition goes missing as fossil fuel language drops from draft deal

events.summary: Explicit references to moving away from fossil fuels were omitted from the latest draft agreement at the COP31 climate summit. Activists highlighted the missing language as the conference neared its scheduled conclusion.
events.why: The omission of fossil fuel transition targets from international climate agreements weakens global emissions reduction commitments.

articles.title: Shattered playgrounds and freezing classrooms: Inside Ukraine’s deadliest year for children

events.summary: UNICEF highlighted that child casualties in Ukraine have reached record levels during the deadliest year of the war for children. Youngsters face compounded hazards from bombings and day-long power cuts amid freezing winter conditions.
events.why: Documenting record casualty figures and infrastructure collapse for children underscores severe humanitarian and human rights crises in Ukraine.

articles.title: Dems aim to block Iran war funding. And, Army delays lead azide detonation in Iowa

events.summary: Congressional Democrats are attempting to leverage upcoming government funding deadlines to block financing for the Iran war. Concurrently, the US Army reported that continuing to delay the detonation of lead azide in Iowa poses growing hazards.
events.why: Efforts to withhold funding could restrict executive war powers and risk a federal government shutdown.

articles.title: Trump threatens ban on US firms building AI data centres overseas
Trump threatens tax on US tech firms building AI data centres abroad

events.summary: The US president has threatened a ban or tax on US tech firms constructing AI data centres overseas. Little detail was provided, and members of his team were reportedly hearing about the potential policy for the first time.
events.why: Restricting where US tech companies can build AI infrastructure could dramatically alter global tech supply chains, energy planning, and foreign investment.

articles.title: Afghanistan restrictions prevent pregnant women from seeking medical help

events.summary: Aid agencies reported that an escalating assault on the rights and freedoms of women and girls in Afghanistan is preventing growing numbers of pregnant women from obtaining essential healthcare.
events.why: Denial of maternal healthcare severely increases preventable maternal and infant mortality across an entire nation.

articles.title: Europe ready for talks with Russia on ending war in Ukraine, leaders say

events.summary: European allies of Ukraine stated they have formed a united negotiating position at a summit in Berlin. They expressed readiness for talks with Russia to end the war.
events.why: A coordinated European negotiating stance marks a pivotal step toward potential formal diplomatic talks to end the war in Ukraine.

articles.title: What are the implications of the ICJ Rohingya genocide ruling?

events.summary: The International Court of Justice issued a genocide verdict against Myanmar regarding the Rohingya. Experts indicate the decision may carry legal precedents affecting Israel's proceedings related to Gaza.
events.why: International Court of Justice genocide rulings set binding legal jurisprudence with broad international ramifications.

articles.title: GOP Sen. Johnson rejects tying government funding to an end to the Iran war

events.summary: Senator Ron Johnson rejected proposals to condition federal government funding on halting the war in Iran. The standoff highlights partisan disagreements as Congress attempts to reach a budget resolution.
events.why: Disagreements over military funding conditions elevate the likelihood of a US government funding lapse.

articles.title: Battle to control GPS and radio signals raises civilian safety concerns

events.summary: Civilian transport including passenger jets, cargo ships, and conflict-zone aid convoys face growing safety risks as GPS and radio signals are increasingly blocked or faked. These disruptions directly undermine safe navigation dependent on satellite systems.
events.why: Widespread electronic warfare and signal spoofing pose systemic threats to international maritime and aviation safety.

articles.title: No government approval needed to form or join a group, UN rights committee says

events.summary: The UN Human Rights Committee issued new formal guidance stating that individuals do not require government permission to form or join associations. The guidance comes amid expanding restrictions on civic space worldwide.
events.why: Official UN human rights guidance clarifies international treaty obligations protecting civil society from state-imposed administrative bans.

articles.title: Indian man sentenced to 19-plus years in plot to assassinate US-based Sikh separatist leader
Indian man sentenced to 19 years in US Sikh separatist assassination plot
Indian man sentenced to 19 years in prison for conspiring to kill Sikh separatist in New York

events.summary: Nikhil Gupta was sentenced to over 19 years in prison after pleading guilty to murder-for-hire and money laundering conspiracies in an assassination plot against a US-based Sikh separatist. The charges followed a February guilty plea regarding the scheme.
events.why: The sentencing establishes legal culpability in an international assassination plot with significant diplomatic friction between the US and India.

articles.title: Sudan’s war leaves disabled children missing out on education

events.summary: The ongoing war in Sudan has forced schools and rehabilitation centers to shut down. Consequently, children with disabilities have lost access to specialized education and support services.
events.why: The breakdown of educational and rehabilitation infrastructure deprives vulnerable children of essential care and developmental support.

articles.title: The U.K. and EU hold a rare summit to strengthen ties

events.summary: Top European Union officials are meeting with Prime Minister Andy Burnham in a rare bilateral summit. The meeting aims to strengthen diplomatic ties ten years after the Brexit referendum.
events.why: Direct EU-UK high-level talks signal a structured effort to renegotiate trade and geopolitical collaboration following Brexit.

articles.title: Putin proposes second humanitarian ceasefire — is it a trap?

events.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin proposed a humanitarian ceasefire to evacuate civilians from Kostiantynivka. Military analysts caution that the proposal could be aimed at advancing strategic tactical goals.
events.why: Ceasefire proposals in actively contested cities directly influence civilian survival and the operational status of frontline warfare.

articles.title: West Bank: Record settler attacks mar olive harvest as UN urges Israel to protect farmers

events.summary: Israeli settlers have carried out more than 400 attacks causing casualties or property damage during this year's olive harvest in the occupied West Bank. UN agencies and NGOs noted this is more than in any previous harvest season.
events.why: Record levels of settler violence directly impact Palestinian agricultural livelihoods and escalate regional instability in the occupied territories.

articles.title: Peacekeeping: With 500 paternity and child support claims unresolved, UN scales up accountability

events.summary: The UN announced new accountability measures to support children fathered by peacekeepers, addressing approximately 500 unresolved paternity and child support claims.
events.why: It establishes administrative accountability and support mechanisms within UN peacekeeping operations for affected families.
